catalog_locator: p. 85 (section 'Tee phonological inventory') and p. 86 Table 3 (PDF pp. 88-89)
catalog_quote: The vowels are also typical of this group. There are 7 oral and 5 nasalized vowels, as illustrated by the words in Table 2. ... all vowels have nasalized allophones when adjacent to nasal consonants. There are three contrasting tones, symbolized as shown in Table 3, with the mid tone being left unmarked. ... Table 3. Contrasting tones in Tee. High bé fight, war / Mid be home / Low bè enclose, make a fence around

audit.action: cite a better source for the same coding
audit.reasoning: (1) Quote check: the deciding sentence and Table 3 are verbatim in the held UCLA WPP 91 scan at the stated pages (p.85 text, p.86 Table 3; scanned pg-088/ plus for the diacritics). (2) The deciding source is a first-hand 1995 phonetic study by Ladefoged, authoritative for what it says (three contrastive level tones, minimal triplet) but only 4 pages and not about prosody, so 'no stress rule described' is an argument from a very short text. (3) Glottolog registers no grammar or sketch for Tee (MED = phonology_or_text); the one open descriptive item beyond Ladefoged, Anyanwu & Omego 2015, was fetched sources now and independently restates the H/M/L system with the same triplet (p.3), adds moraic syllable structure and prefix-triggered tone spreading, and never mentions stress or accent -- it confirms the 'tonal' coding and shows tone is lexically and morphologically contrastive.

sources.citation: Anyanwu, Ogbonna and Christie Omego. 2015. Aspects of Deverbal Nominalization in Tee. In Ruth Kramer, Elizabeth C. Zsiga and One Tlale Boyer (eds.), Selected Proceedings of the 44th Annual Conference on African Linguistics, 1-10. Somerville, MA: Cascadilla Proceedings Project (document #3121).
sources.quote: "There are three phonemic tones which are high, mid and low as shown by the following words which display tonal contrast. 5a) be 'fight (noun)' b) be 'home' c) be 'fence'" ... "In Tee, a syllable may be either mono-moraic or polymoraic." The rest of the paper describes M- and L-tone spreading from nominalizing prefixes onto H-tone verb roots. The words 'stress' and 'accent' occur nowhere in the paper (grep: 0 hits).
sources.locator: p.3, section 1, examples (5a-c) and following paragraph on syllable structure; tone-spreading rules pp.4-9
sources.note: Independent native-region linguists' description restating the three-tone system (p.3) with tone-spreading rules and syllable/mora structure; corroborates the Ladefoged-based 'tonal' coding and shows tone is lexical and morphologically active. fetched sources now.
